outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Positional Encoding in Transformers
outline.description: This chapter introduces the role of position embeddings in Transformer‑based language models, focusing on the Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) that is ubiquitous in modern LLMs. It explains the mathematical formulation of RoPE, how rotation angles are computed from token indices and frequency parameters, and why positional information is essential for capturing sequential dependencies.
subtopics: Introduction to sequence modeling and the need for explicit position information
The RoPE formulation: cosine/sine rotations and frequency scaling
Base value of θ and its effect on embedding range
Comparison with other positional encodings (absolute, sinusoidal)
Implications of RoPE for attention computations

outline.chapter_title: Motivation: The Challenge of Ultra‑Long Context Windows
outline.description: This chapter motivates the problem by summarizing practical limitations of existing LLMs (e.g., 4096 token windows) and why extending context length is desirable for downstream tasks. It discusses the three main obstacles to ultra‑long windows: catastrophic new positions, lack of training data, and attention dispersion.
subtopics: Use‑cases requiring >10⁴ tokens (in‑context learning, agents, document summarization)
Catastrophic positions: distributional shift and out‑of‑distribution behavior
Attention dilution in large windows and its effect on downstream performance
Existing upper bounds (~128k) and their limitations

outline.description: This chapter surveys conventional strategies that have been applied to extend context windows: linear interpolation (PI), NTK‑based interpolation, dynamic NTK, YaRN, and others. It presents each method’s intuition, implementation details, and known trade‑offs.
subtopics: Linear Positional Interpolation (PI) – scaling down angles uniformly
NTK‑based Interpolation and Extrapolation – frequency‑aware scaling
YaRN – group‑wise treatment of RoPE dimensions
Strengths and weaknesses across target extensions
